column4: Work-type lookup has unknown security and only Id, Title and CreatedOn fields.
Creating a nongroup pad requires an API key but has no explicit owner, role or membership authorization rule.
Notification subscriptionType describes notification routing rather than a required subscription tier; security is unknown.
Candidate history is descriptive electoral data but supplied API-key requirements do not establish unrestricted access.
Private article update contains authors and group_id without a verified account-owner binding or caller access rule.
Notification-export detail has unknown security and lacks owner or tenant relationships.
API-key user_id is response-derived and permission_set is opaque, leaving mutation authorization and lookup unresolved.
Automation has user_id, user_ids and group_ids without evidence selecting individual or group authorization.
Payment customer and merchant identifiers describe transaction data but do not establish caller ownership.
Current-user profile is self-scoped but has no input object identifier; public_profile OAuth scope does not make the endpoint public.
Collaborator ACL flags and sharingKey imply multiple possible access paths without a supported verified ownership or role policy.
Score track creator is provenance, while sharingKey and OAuth permissions do not establish a single owner lookup.
Summary explicitly filters favorite photos by caller permission, so Public tag does not justify unrestricted access.
Group topic listing is tagged Public but privacy metadata and unknown effective security leave unrestricted access unproven.
Person response mixes public and private-looking user fields; Public tag alone cannot resolve caller authorization.
Photo visibility, owner and permissions indicate conditional access; Public tag does not establish unrestricted retrieval.
Expiring a PDF submission requires token Basic authentication but lacks a supplied submission-owner relation.
Game admin billing path suggests privilege but does not explicitly establish a caller role or game ownership binding.
Private-space invitation requires collaborator OAuth scope, not a proven application role, and ERD lacks ownership mapping.
Space modification has collaborator, owner and robot scopes without verified roles or a space-owner lookup.
Creating an API version has unknown security and only descriptive version fields.
Linked API relations include generated example keys without a verified caller access relationship.
Similar-image retrieval uses API-key or OAuth authentication without affirmative unrestricted-access evidence.
Admin hook retrieval has several authentication alternatives but no explicit caller role or verified object binding.
Notification response includes repository owner, permissions and recipient, leaving the actual notification access relationship ambiguous.
Organization label retrieval has org context but no tenant column or verified caller-organization mapping.
Git-hook retrieval has owner in the path but no owner relationship in the returned hook fields.
Repository-hook editing uses owner path context without a verified repository-owner lookup or admin-bypass evidence.
Installation-token permissions describe granted capabilities, not the caller authorization required to mint the token.
Scoped-token response mixes account, user and installation permissions without verified caller authorization semantics.
Gist comments include author details but no affirmative public-access statement or verified ownership requirement.
Updating a gist comment exposes author data but does not specify owner-only editing or a verified lookup.
Ad-exchange account update has buyer OAuth scopes but no verified caller-account ownership or tenant mapping.
Billing accountId is a response-derived account hint that does not distinguish individual ownership from tenant authorization.
Budget update uses accountId and billingId without a verified relationship to caller identity.
Newsletter image retrieval has unknown security and no affirmative unrestricted-access statement.
Account-role record includes user and manager flags but does not define the caller's required role or ownership rule.
Notifying an account-role object has token authentication without a verified account/user access relationship.
Account owner and managers are inferred response fields, insufficient to select owner-only versus tenant authorization.
Account-manager listing has account context but no caller-account binding in manager contact fields.
Starting an account payment setup intent provides only payment_method_id, not an ownership lookup.
Device-rule listing requires bearer authentication but returns only pagination and data wrappers.
Certificate-action listing has unknown security and no ownership fields in pagination response data.
Government campaign metadata has unknown API security and no affirmative unrestricted-access statement.
Tagged media retrieval supplies pagination metadata without explicit public access or caller authorization evidence.
Organization-model lookup is administration-tagged but has no explicit caller role or tenant lookup relationship.
API-key privilege listing authenticates the request but pagination fields do not reveal the authorized caller relationship.
Organization billing positions have tenant-like path context but only billing amounts in ERD.
Document ownerOrganizationId and sharing visibility are inferred hints without a verified organization lookup or authorization rule.
Address extraction includes an api_key query parameter but unknown security and no explicit unrestricted-access evidence.
